claims.claim: Apollinaris of Laodicea, also known as Apollinaris the Younger, was a bishop of Laodicea in Syria.
Apollinaris the Younger was born c. 310 and died c. 390.
Apollinaris was a noted opponent of Arianism.
Apollinaris's eagerness to emphasize the deity of Jesus and the unity of his person led him to deny the existence of a rational human soul in Christ's human nature, a view called Apollinarism.
Apollinarism was condemned by the First Council of Constantinople in 381.

Apollinaris collaborated with his father, Apollinaris the Elder, in reproducing the Old Testament in the form of Homeric and Pindaric poetry and the New Testament after the fashion of Platonic dialogues, when the emperor Julian had forbidden Christians to teach the classics.
Apollinaris was elected bishop c. 361 by the Nicene community of Laodicea.
Apollinaris lectured at Antioch c. 374, where St. Jerome was one of his auditors.
Apollinaris was renowned for his logical mind and knowledge of Hebrew.
